definitions.explanation: Describes something kept clean and free of germs in a way that protects health. The opposite is {非衛生的|ひえいせいてき} (unsanitary).

examples.japanese: {衛生的|えいせいてき}な{環境|かんきょう}。
{台所|だいどころ}はいつも{衛生的|えいせいてき}に{保|たも}ちたい。
examples.english: I want to always keep the kitchen hygienic.

examples.japanese: {食|た}べ{物|もの}を{扱|あつか}う{店|みせ}は、{衛生的|えいせいてき}であることが{何|なに}より{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: For shops that handle food, being hygienic is more important than anything.

notes:
Composed of {衛生|えいせい} (hygiene, sanitation) + the suffix {的|てき} (-ical). A na-adjective describing conditions that are clean and healthy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {衛生的|えいせいてき}な{環境|かんきょう}: a sanitary environment
- {衛生的|えいせいてき}に{保|たも}つ: to keep something hygienic
- {衛生的|えいせいてき}な{処理|しょり}: hygienic handling

USAGE:
The negative {非衛生的|ひえいせいてき} (unsanitary) is common. To say something is simply 'clean,' {清潔|せいけつ} is more everyday; {衛生的|えいせいてき} stresses freedom from germs and health risks.
